  https://ei-study.atlassian.net/browse/EIT-8403
- EIT-8383 – Enhance the OpenAPI spec writer skill with lessons from the consolidated services' OpenAPI refinements
  https://ei-study.atlassian.net/browse/EIT-8383
Confluence: https://ei-study.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~712020ceae13b03d30455ebc4ce41736ab9dd0/pages/2303230002

In short: billing profiles (GSTIN, TAN, card, billing name and address) and the per-user credit wallet moved from Identity Service to Billing Service. Code, OpenAPI, tests, the gateway, canon-data and the remote databases are updated, and account numbers are now encrypted at rest. Four repos are pushed. The portal UI change is ready but not committed. Nothing is deployed yet. Separately, the OpenAPI spec writer skill now carries the lessons from the OpenAPI refinements. It is pushed but not yet tried on a real spec.

1. Done today
   1. EIT-8403 – Moved billing details and user credits from Identity to Billing
      - Billing now holds each tenant's account and billing details (GST, TAN, card, billing name and address) and each user's credit balance. Before, these lived in Identity.
      - The account numbers are now stored encrypted. Before, they were stored as plain text.
      - A tenant user can only see and change their own tenant's billing details. Our internal staff can see all tenants.
      - Identity no longer has these features. Its old code, tables and documentation were removed.
      - The gateway now sends these requests to Billing. When a user is deleted, their credits are also removed from Billing.
      - The Portal app now reads and saves account details from Billing. If Billing is unavailable, it shows a warning instead of an empty screen.
      - The shared data dictionary (canon-data) and the API documentation are updated to match.
   2. Moved the data on the shared server
      - Took backups first.
      - Copied the 3 credit balances and their 3 history entries into Billing, and checked that the copies match exactly.
      - Removed the old tables from Identity.
      - The 2 account records in Identity were dummy test data, so we did not copy them.
   3. Fixed existing problems found along the way
      - Billing: cleaned up code-style and documentation errors, and raised test coverage above the required level.
      - Identity: fixed all code-style warnings.
      - Identity: fixed a real security bug. A one-time login code (OTP) could be used twice if two requests arrived at the same moment. It now works only once.
   4. EIT-8383 – Updated open api spec writing skill in ei-factory-mcp
      - The skill now checks the actual code before writing, follows each project's existing style, and applies the writing rules that is agreed on discussion with rahul.
      - Implementation is done, but needs to test the updated skills with multiple models.

9. Learnings
   1. Check what is actually in the database before planning a migration. Identity's credit and account tables only ever held seed rows. The real data is in legacy, which changes what "moving the data" means.
   2. A flaky test can hide a real bug. The flaky OTP test was a real double-use race in production code.
   3. Columns named *_encrypted were storing plain text in identity. Names prove nothing; the code does.
   4. Canon drift can start on day one. billing_name and client_type were copied from legacy validators when canon was created and never matched the new schemas.

      - Ran background agents for the coverage tests and the identity lint / OTP fix.
      - Ran the remote DB steps with read-only checks before each change.
   3. Quality checks:

      - Checksums equal on the remote copy.
      - canon-data validate + gate self-test.
      - Spec description edits approved line by line before editing, following openapi-spec-writing-guide.md.
